1. Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned AGA and perused the record.
No one appears for the opposite party no.2 despite notice.

2. The accused-applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No.161 of 2017 under sections 363, 328, 376-D,
506, 120-B IPC and section 5/6 POCSO Act and section 3(2)(v) SC/ST Act, P.S. Satrikh, District Barabanki.
3.
The FIR in question was filed on 23.05.2017 alleging that the victim was going to her aunt's place on 22.05.2017 and he sat on a passenger train at about 02:00 pm and she slept.
It was further Manish Kumar vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko.

alleged that she got down at Barabanki Station where she met with two persons and as they told that her brother was at brick kiln, the victim went along with the said two persons.
It was further stated that the victim was taken to a place where her jeans was removed and as she shouted, many people came and they ran away.
She also specifically stated that nothing wrong was done to her.
No one was named in the FIR.
4. In the statement under section 161 Cr.P.C., the victim reiterated the said version.
She also stated that on 18.05.2017 she was unhappy with her parents and she went out of her own.
She also stated that she had gone with the applicant and two other persons on a truck.
She specifically stated that nothing wrong was done to her.
The medical of the victim was done on 24.05.2017 which do not corroborate any allegations of wrong being committed on her.
However, in the statement under section 164 Cr.P.C., the victim stated that she was taken by three co-accused including the applicant on a truck.
She also stated that she was administered liquor and thereafter wrong was committed on her.
The tentative age of the victim has been assessed as 15 years.
5. It is argued that no charge-sheet was filed against the applicant, however, the applicant has been summoned in exercise of the power under section 319 Cr.P.C.
It is further argued that the co-accused against whom the charge-sheet has been filed, has already been convicted.
6. Learned AGA opposed the bail application.

7. Considering the huge variance in the allegations contained in the FIR and the two statements under sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. and there being no material whatsoever to corroborate the allegations and the fact that the applicant was summoned in exercise of the power under section 319 Cr.P.C., prima-facie a case for bail is made out more so when the applicant has no criminal history and is in custody since 02.04.2024.
Thus the bail application is allowed.

8. Let the applicant Manish Kumar be released on bail in aforesaid first information report number subject to his furnishing a personal bond and two reliable sureties of Rs.20,000/- (Twenty Thousand) each of the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
Order Date :- 15.7.2024 VNP/-
Manish Kumar vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko.
